These constitute the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
Fourth, the lightness of noble lineage;
first, the traces of the former fisherman’s virtue;
and the source of goodness—these are the four.
Third, one dwells in a corrupt and evil place;
fourth, one is born under calamity and raised without seeing [one's parents];
these are the three.
Fourth is reflection on past conduct. These four—
reflection on the North Star, reflection on the North Pole, reflection on the traces of the Worthy One,
and long breathing— are the four.
The five are: being gentle and supple;
having keen hearing; craving wealth; being honored as a source of a hundred poisons; and being the root and origin.
These constitute the five.
Fourth is the treatment of karma through the constellations.
Under the constellation Hastā (the Elephant), one performs painting and the pouring of consecrated liquids;
this constitutes the fourth.
As for those four lunar mansions,
they preside over urgent and calamitous matters;
they are named Mṛgaśiras, Citrā, and Aśvinī.
These constitute the four [groups].
Among these twenty-eight lunar mansions,
three mansions lead the way in front as guides.
The moon travels ahead,
while the stars follow behind;
this is called "guiding and leading."
What are these three?
They are the Āśvalāyana, the Aśvaka, and the Pūrvaśaila;
furthermore, there are the twelve lunar mansions (nakṣatras).
He attended upon [his elders].

Shan Yuan and Shan Ge delighted their superiors; Gen Yuan was like a fish following another fish; Er Cong was greedy for wealth; Qian Xian left traces to the north; and Xian Ji allowed no room for others.
These are the twelve.
As companions to the moon,
there are twelve lunar mansions.
Fame, growth, birth of deer-headed offspring, increase of calamities, increase of wealth, flourishing prosperity, failure to visit one's local deity, and obtaining an elephant before one's time—
these are the twelve,
each having its own presiding influence.
Seven planetary spirits manifest portents and cause disturbances.
What are these seven?
Qingbai presides over the house;
Sizili is the lord of the waters.
Huo (Fire), Huozhu (Lord of Fire),
Yao (Medicine), Yaokhanji (Tranquil Medicine), and Asura;
these are the seven distinct lunar mansions.
Puṇṇa Kassapa asked again:
"Having dwelt in the world during previous lives,
how did you proceed?"
Peaceful and harmonious are the days and nights.
How can they be made long?
How can they be made short?
King Māndhātṛ said:
"In the winter month, on the eighth day,
there are eighteen muhūrtas in the night."
During the day there are exactly twelve *muhūrta*;
on the eighth day of the fourth month of spring,
however, the day consists of only eighteen *muhūrta*.
The night consists of twelve *muhūrta*;
it corresponds to the seventh day of summer,
when the eighth day is due.
The day consists of fifteen muhūrtas,
and the night likewise consists of fifteen muhūrtas.
He asked again:
What constitutes a "section"?
What constitutes a "limit"?
What constitutes a "momentary interval"?
King Māndhātṛ said:
"It is like a person cutting three feet of thread that is neither too long nor too short."
These are called "joints" (*parvan*).
Calculating sixty joints,
they are termed "limits" (*maryādā*).
Twelve *kṣaṇas* are reckoned as one *muhūrta*. Calculated in this manner,
[the day and night consist of thirty such units].
Day and night pass by.
Furthermore, there are thirty kṣaṇas [in a muhūrta].
Again, he asked.
"What are the names of these various moments?
He replied:
When the sun first rises,
a person's own form measures nine zhang and six chi.
That moment is called a *muhūrta*;
a shadow of six feet [in length] constitutes one *muhūrta*.
It is named Victory (Jaya).
It is one zhang and two chi tall,
and its shadow shifts in an instant.
The one named Fu-le (Abundance and Joy) has a shadow six chi long for a brief moment;
the one named Wo-shou (Lying Head) [is likewise].
A shadow of five chi for a brief moment is called Fu'an;
a shadow of four chi for a brief moment—
The one named Free from Pleasure has a shadow of three feet that lasts but a moment;
the one named Equal Good Face—
The brief interval at midday is called Vajra;
the brief interval after midday is...
The first period is called *Lìhē* (Vilakṣa);
when the shadow is four feet long, it is briefly called *Qiángliǎng* (Balavat).
The second period is when the shadow is five feet long.
The first moment is named "Attaining Victory" (Jaya).
The shadow of six chi is named "All Real" (Sarvatattva) for a brief moment.
The shadow of one zhang two chi is [the next] brief moment.
The first is named Jizhe (Treatise on Karma);
the second, after six *zhàng*,
is named Sharen (Virtuous Benevolence).
At the first moment of sunset, when the shadow is nine zhang and six chi long,
it is called "Most Relaxed," yet one still harbors fear.
Now I shall speak:
it was but a short while ago at night,
and but a short while after the sun had set.
The first is named "Vicious and Wicked.
The second brief interval is named "Exquisite Woman."
The next is named Kulanāman;
the next is named Upanāman;
the next is named Anantanāman.
Next is called "Donkey's Cry";
next is called "Evil Ghost.
At the brief moment of midnight, [these sounds occur].
It is named Āma;
after half a moment has passed,
it is named Brahma.
The next is named Colorful Painting;
the next is named No Attachment;
the next is named Abandoning Thought.
The next is named Anala;
the next is named Agni;
the next is named Agnija.
This day and night consists of thirty *muhūrtas*.
King Māndhātṛ said:
Furthermore, listen again as I distinguish these for you, O Benevolent One:
there are fifteen types of winks.
This is called a *tsu* (instant).
Twenty *tsu* constitute one *i* (unit of time).
Thirty *i* are called a *su-yü* (moment).
Thirty *muhūrta* constitute one day and night;
thirty days constitute one month;
and twelve months are calculated as one year.
Summing the nights and days of the year, including the bright and the blinking [periods],
there are one hundred and sixty million and fifty;
this is the calculation for distinguishing the divisions of time.
King Mātaṅga said:
"O Brahmin, listen to the measurement of yojanas and li:
seven *paramāṇus* constitute one *anu*."
Seven *anū* make one particle of dust in a window;
seven particles of dust in a window make one particle of dust on a hare’s fur.
Seven particles on a rabbit constitute one particle on a sheep;
seven particles on a sheep [constitute one particle on an ox].
Seven particles on a cow constitute one particle on a cow;
seven such particles on a cow then constitute one nit.
Seven *kṛmi* (nits) combined constitute one *yūka* (louse);
seven *yūka* constitute one *yava* (barley grain);
and seven *yava* constitute one finger-joint (*aṅguliparvan*).
Twelve finger-joints make one *śukti*;
two *śukti* make one *hasta*;
four *hasta* make one long bow (*dhanus*).
One thousand bows constitute one *śabda*.
Thirty *li* constitute one *yojana*.
[There are] three hundred and ten million.
One thousand six hundred billion;
fourteen billion;
five hundred million.
Twelve thousand *mī* (yojanas) combine to form one *yojana*.
This is the detailed analysis of the origin and extent of the measurement of *li*.
King Mātaṅga said,
"Three and a half *liǎng* are reckoned as one unit;
this is the standard of measurement used in the kingdom of Magadha."
One *dundubhisvara* is equal to eight hundred and forty-seven million,
seven thousand and eighty *muhūrtas*.
This constitutes one *pīla*.
Now, furthermore, listen as I distinguish the various measures of flavor:
twelve *jin* of clarified butter (*ghṛta*) constitutes one measure.
In the kingdom of Magadha,
one *sheng* [measures] seventy *jin* of honey;
thus, one *sheng* is minute.
A total of two billion three hundred million,
two million nine hundred seventy thousand,
four thousand seven hundred and twenty *mī* (micro-units).
This constitutes one *dǒngshèng*.
This is the calculation for flavors.
Now, listen as I distinguish the various grains and rice.
Ten jin constitute one sheng in the kingdom of Magadha;
calculating from the minute unit upward,
it amounts to twelve billion eight hundred million.
Two hundred twenty-six thousand,
one thousand five hundred and thirty *mī* (micro-units) constitute one *sheng* (dry measure).
This was his analysis of the fundamental insignificance of rice and grain.
Fu Jia-sha asked again:

He replied, "I have simply understood it.

his fame reached far and wide."

one born under the constellation Mṛgaśiras will delight in fighting, strife, and litigation.

One born on the day of the constellation Zengcai (Zengcai) will increase their wealth.
He delights in farming, plowing, and sowing;
he was born under the constellation Chideng (Jyesthā);
and he upholds and protects the prohibitive precepts.
One born under the constellation *Sudhāna* is not seen [by others];
one born under *Pūrvaphalgunī* is negligent and full of desire;
one born under *Uttaraphalgunī* is a ruler of land.
One will attain great wealth and nobility.
Those born on the day of the former virtue (Puṣya) will have meager fortune and short lives.
He was born in Beide County.
By nature, he observed the fasts and precepts and protected the True Dharma.
May you be reborn in a favorable realm.
One born under the lunar mansion of Hastā is by nature fond of theft.
Born under the constellation Citrā,
he delights in adorning himself and in music, song, and dance.
He was born under the constellation Shan-yuan and was likewise of meager fortune; moreover,
he was skilled at calculating and writing.
Those born on the day of the Xiù star will be skilled at measuring and calculating;
they will belong to the local magistracy,
or serve as officials and soldiers.
Those born on the day of Joyful Accord (Ratana) are inclined toward commerce,
trade, and seeking profit through buying and selling.
Those born on the day of Honorable Elder (Sujāta) are respectful toward their elders and seniors.
They will likewise have short lifespans and possess little wealth or occupation;
their roots and origins were born from past lives.
Furthermore, he had many children,
and his fame for virtue spread far and wide.
He was born under the constellation of Matsya (the Fish).
Delighting in dwelling in seclusion,
one attains concentration through solitary practice.
One born under the constellation Bei Yu (Pisces).
The artisan immediately mounted his horse and became proficient in the five weapons;
it was impossible for such skill to have been born overnight.
He was renowned from his youth;
his courage and prowess were unsurpassed,
and he possessed the keen hearing born of past lives.
He will be honored and respected by the royal household;
his greed for wealth arises from past lives;
he is stubborn and difficult to transform.
Stubborn and self-opinionated,
they know no shame or remorse;
a hundred poisons arise within them day by day.
He delighted in practicing the arts of medicine, talismans, and incantations,
as well as illusions and the way of sorcery (gudao).
These were traces left by former sages arising from his past lives.
He delighted in acting as a leader of bandits,
plundering the innocent.
He was born on the day of Xianjiexiu in the north.
He delighted in music and was skilled at playing the five tones;
he was born on the day of Liuguan (the ninth day of the lunar month).
One born on the day of the Horse Nakṣatra often becomes a boatman or a horse trainer,
and always delights in tending horses.
Those born under the constellation Chángxī (Long-sigh) will take pleasure in acting as executioners or butchers.
This is the detailed analysis of the origins and characteristics of the various constellations.
Pukkusa further asked King Mātaṅga:
"Your Majesty, are you able to know how to determine the proper placement of land according to the constellations?
He replied: "I have studied it somewhat."
He asked again, "What does this mean?
and then spoke in verse:
"The fame established by the Sun, That city is most majestic."
Possessing many rare treasures, yet later consumed by fire;
having long nurtured what was previously produced, and having accumulated vast wealth,
one who possesses wise intelligence delights in giving and upholds the precepts.
In the city established by Mṛgaśiras, there will be many women, cattle, wealth, flowers, garments,
and various foods and drinks; though it flourishes for a short time, it will eventually disperse and give rise to calamities,
yet it was founded by a constellation and abounds in food, drink, and treasures.
The people of that land were debased and evil; Foolish and obscured, they lacked wisdom.

Though their wealth was increased by what had been established in the past, And the city flourished with towering splendor, With riches, grain, and crops in great abundance, As soon as it reached such plenty, it fell into ruin.
Established by the constellation Jyeṣṭhā, that city is lofty in virtue;
its wealth and grain are abundant, and it delights in sacrifice.
Its food is plentiful yet lacks flavor, and because it does not behold the constellation established there, it is mostly impoverished and fond of strife and change.
Dwelling in suffering, he was cast aside; such was the state of the people.
On this land established from of old, the high-minded man of great wealth supported his wife, and there was a place for him to offer sacrifices.
In the north, established by the former virtue of Puṣya, women delight in floral ornaments, incense, and various treasures; its fulfillment of the mind is thus.
In the north, established by the former virtue of Puṣya, there are many precious jewels and grains.
Men lie prostrate before women; the city upon which they rely is so called because it was established under the lunar mansion Citrā.
Its inhabitants are impoverished yet possess great wealth, and they take pleasure in coveting the property of others—such are the people of that land.
Adorned with colorful paintings, established by the constellation Svāti;
the women are most excellent, abundant in jewels, and always foremost in music.
Then, though afflicted by fire, it is established by the constellation Puṣya; wealth and undertakings flourish everywhere.
The people are corrupt, wicked, and foolish; their nature is mostly like that of donkeys and horses.
They are skilled at debating and established in their former positions;
their city’s virtue is lofty and majestic, and many people delight in making offerings there. Only then will it be destroyed by war.
Delighting in what was established by his ancestors, subduing the senses and honoring the prohibitions of the Dharma,
he protected his wife; performing sacrifices at the proper times without fail,
he respected his elders and inherited the rare treasures and abundant wealth established by his ancestors.
He was extensively learned in the classics, and his roots of faith increased day by day.
Originally established in a land abundant with rare treasures and teeming with people that was difficult to withstand, he was destroyed by the rain of dust.
Established in the former Fish mansion, there will be abundance of wealth and grain;
yet people will be stingy, greedy, and cruel, returning once more to folly.
Established in the northern Fish mansion, wealth, enterprises, and the five grains will flourish.
A person who understands the arts of medicine, whose disposition is ever free from strife,
whose hearing is acute as established by past karma, and who possesses abundant wealth and grain—
though such a person may live in peace with few ailments, they will nonetheless be ruined by disease.
Those established by the constellation Greedy Wealth (Ārdrā) are of the earth element;
they appear as women and mostly wear garments adorned with flowers and colorful patterns.
Those established by the constellation Abandoning Affection (Punarvasu) have no room for the karma of worldly attachment; their city is always difficult to conquer.
The people are courageous and fierce, their majestic splendor ever sublime.
Though many poisons have long been established there, the local inhabitants are shrouded in darkness;
they delight in lewd women, wine, and sensual beauty, and in the end, they shall be ravaged by water.
The traces established by former sages: when people’s wealth and undertakings are in harmony, yet they are foolish and corrupt, offending against the wives of others;
those who delight in darkness and arrogance—these are the traces of the northern sages. Day by day there is benefit.
Wealth, grain, and crops are abundant; one delights in giving and upholds the precepts.
The waters flow through the lands established by former merits;
the local people enjoy adornment, and there are many camels, donkeys, and mules. Wealth, grain, and crops are plentiful.
In lands established by the Master of Horses, the territory is exceedingly prosperous;
people are peaceful and free from affliction, their countenances upright and beautiful.
In lands established by the Long-Breather, the soil is impoverished and strife is common.

When one’s precepts are ruined or lost through calamity, and the land is in such a state, if one wishes to establish a kingdom, cities, or dwellings, one should examine the constellations and the seasons;
only when auspiciousness is protected may construction begin. In my past lives, I studied in this manner.
King Māndhātṛ said to Pukkasāti,
"This is the detailed exposition of the origins and endings of various past lives."
The brahmin asked again,
"Venerable sir, have you also studied the rain-staying rite?
He replied, "I have mastered it."
Let us first explain the gains and losses regarding the rain.
King Māndhātṛ said:
"In the past, my fame was such that..."
In the fifth month, it began to rain;
when it reached nine *hu*,
ten days had passed.
In the sixth and seventh months,
it was likewise so;
there was abundant growth and flourishing.
The five grains ripen in abundance;
there is little water in autumn and winter.
At that time, they sow by fire.
It will spontaneously burn.
On the day of long growth,
there will be rain in the fifth month.
The yield fell by three *shu* and one and a half *sheng*.
High-lying fields suffered from drought,
while low-lying fields managed to harvest a crop.
The harvests did not ripen.
At that time, there were two kinds of ailments:
the first was eye disease.
The second is abdominal pain.
Thieves will flourish.
This is the day presided over by the constellation Mṛgaśiras.
In the fifth month, rain fell;
nine hu and six sheng were dropped.
The five grains ripened in abundance.
If the kingdom remains hidden and concealed,
and weapons are not deployed,
all nations will be at peace and secure.
Regarding those who are without misfortune or distress:
on the day of one's birth star,
or on the fifth month when it rains for the first time.
The harvest fell short by two hu and seven sheng;
the high fields yielded nothing,
while the low fields were lush and abundant.
One must urgently prepare and store provisions. Why is this?
Because there are many thieves and robbers.
At that time, when the various kings raise their armies and mobilize their troops,
there will be four calamities.
First is coughing disease;
second is upward breath (asthma);
third is wind-induced itching.
The fourth is the fever disease,
which frequently harms young children;
it is associated with the constellation Zengcai (Jyeṣṭhā).
In the fifth month, rain fell;
thirteen hu and an additional five sheng were dropped.
From the fifth month until the eighth month,
all kings shall conceal their weapons and implements of war,
and all shall possess a heart of compassion.
No harm shall come from thieves;
the days will be blazing hot,
and there will be rain at the beginning of the fifth month.
It fell four hu and eight sheng;
the high fields did not flourish,
while the low fields were lush and abundant.
Various heterodox practitioners delight in mutual strife and contention;
elephants and tigers are fierce and harmful.
On the day before the full moon of the fifth month, rain fell,
amounting to three hu, one dou, and five sheng.
If there is anyone who knows,
they shall not plow the high fields,
but shall instead plow the low fields.
The winds and rains were untimely;
the king harbored malice,
and all was discordant and lacking harmony.
Although it rained heavily at that time,
the five grains flourished,
yet husband and wife were not in harmony.
Frequent joy in strife;
the ancient days of the land;
rain in the fifth month.
It will yield nine hu and six sheng.
During the year, there will be heavy rains,
and the five grains will ripen to full maturity.
At that time, women, birds, sheep,
and livestock gradually began to suffer miscarriages,
and many people died.
According to the records of former virtuous masters,
on the first day of the fifth month, five years ago,
it rained nine *hu* and six *sheng*.
The five grains flourished,
and although there was a good harvest that year,
bandits came from distant regions.
They oppressed the land,
causing it to find no peace;
they indulged themselves excessively in food and drink.
May humans and animals in the womb be forever free from suffering and hardship.
This was recorded on a day of past virtue in the north.
In the fifth month, rain fell;
twelve hu, nine dou, and one sheng were dropped.
The five grains flourished in abundance.
The armies of various nations shall lay down their weapons;
blades shall not be raised,
and the people shall dwell in peace and security.
As for those who are never exhausted:
the various brahmins delight in engaging in mutual strife and contention.
On the day of the lunar mansion Hastā,
in the fifth month, it rained,
falling seven *shu*, three *dou*, and five *sheng*.
Thereupon, it ceased;
the harvest of that year was poor,
and the five grains were not abundant.
The people suffer from famine.
On the day of the constellation *Svāti*,
it rains in the fifth month.
Nine hu and six dou fell [as rain].
The five grains ripened in abundance.
At that time, the various kingdoms withdrew their troops and laid down their weapons.
The blade of the sword was not drawn;
all was peaceful and free from harm.
This was on an auspicious day of long-standing merit.
In the fifth month, rain fell,
totaling three *shu*, one *dou*, and five *sheng*.
There were also many winds.
At that time, bandits rose up;
the days were auspicious for archery,
and it rained in the fifth month.
Twelve hu of grain fell [as a harvest].
During that year, there was heavy rain,
and the five grains flourished.
When the various kingdoms become powerful and prosperous,
there will be fires and many elephants will die.
It was pleasing that it rained on the fifth day of the fifth month;
nine *hu* of rain fell.
At that time, all five grains shall ripen to maturity,
and one's relatives and friends shall be strong and healthy.
On the day before the anniversary of the Venerable One’s passing, on the fifth month,
it rained two hu and four dou.
One should not cultivate the field again. Why is this?
What is sown will not grow.
It frequently harms young children;
when external bandits come in a violent manner,
it causes loss and destruction.
On the day of the Root (Mūla) lunar mansion,
on the fifth month, it rained;
nine *hu* and six *dou* fell.
The five grains will flourish in abundance,
yet thieves and bandits will be powerful;
at that time, there will be three types of disease.
First is pain in the throat;
second is pain in the flanks;
third is eye disease.
The flowers and fruits flourished luxuriantly.
At that time, the various kings laid down their weapons and armor.
It was forever without any contrivance.
On the day before the fish had been kept overnight,
it rained on the fifth day of the fifth month.
Nine hu and six dou fell [of grain].
The five grains flourished and grew luxuriantly during the sixth and seventh months.
When there is a great flood,
two diseases arise:
the first is called eye pain.
The second is called "Recurring Pain.
On the day of the Fish lunar mansion (Mīna),
it rains in the fifth month.
It will yield fifteen hu;
it is not suitable for low-lying fields,
but should be cultivated on high ground.
When it rains heavily from the heavens and the rivers overflow,
there occurs a water disaster.
The lower fields were ruined by flooding,
while the high fields flourished alone;
at that time, there were three kinds of disease.
First is throat disease;
second is pain in the navel;
third is wind-induced itching.
On the day of the *suǒdì* (宿日) lunar mansion,
on the fifth month, rain fell for five days,
yielding nine *hù* and six *dǒu*.
The heavens send down rain,
the five grains ripen and mature,
and the various dragons dwelling in the waters [prosper].
Ghosts, spirits, birds,
and beasts all suffered calamities;
pestilence spread extensively.
At that time, the various kingdoms raised their armies and mobilized their troops;
they were greedy for wealth from days past,
and on the first day of the fifth month, it rained.
It yields seven *hu*, six *dou*, and five *sheng*.
When it rains there, the heavens send rain neither too much nor too little,
so that even inferior fields obtain a harvest.
When the high fields yield little,
there arises one affliction,
namely the disease of wounds and sores.
When the kings of various nations prepare their weapons and armaments,
when the hundred poisons lie dormant,
and on the day of the fifth month's first rain.
Three hu and four dou will be lost;
one should cultivate the low-lying fields,
but not plow the high-lying fields.
The grain harvests will not flourish;
at that time, the people will be terrified and live in insecurity.
Cradling their children, they fled in terror.
This was on the day preceding the anniversary of the Former Sage’s passing;
it was the first rain of the fifth month.
It fell nine *hu* and six *dou*.
First there was a drought on the first day of the fifth month;
later, there was a great flood.
There will be disasters regarding the five grains and various flowers and fruits;
when rain falls,
enemies and bandits will flourish.
There will then be two ailments:
first, heart pain;
second, feverish illness.
The ministers will be in discord;
elephants and livestock will die.
This is the day of the lunar mansion Xiánjí (Jyeṣṭhā) in the north.
In the fifth month, rain fell;
fifteen hu fell,
and the lower fields could not be harvested.
Heavy rains overflowed,
and the floods breached the city walls and endangered the settlements.
At that time, there were four diseases:
first, cough; second, fever;
third, boils; and fourth, a sallow complexion.
The fourth is the eye disease;
it frequently harms young children and causes the death of elephants and livestock.
The flowers and fruits were both flourishing;
water flowed and irrigated them for several days,
and on the first day of the fifth month, it rained.
It fell nine hu and five dou;
although there was heavy rain,
the five grains flourished in abundance.
The family lived in harmony,
and they delighted one another with food and drink, as well as with their relatives and friends.
The armies of various nations were withdrawn;
bounty and virtue were distributed;
and the stars and constellations moved in their proper courses.
On the day of the horse-master (Jiazi) in the fifth month, it rained,
falling seven *hu* and two *dou*.
There was drought last month,
and subsequently there was drought again;
yet the low-lying fields yielded abundant harvests.
The high fields did not yield,
but the barley, wheat,
rice, and millet all ripened.
The rice and grain do not flourish;
the men of various nations are valiant,
training in arms and adorning themselves for war.
The enemy rebels are powerful and flourishing;
they have occupied the land for many days.
On the first day of the fifth month, it rained.
Fifteen hu of grain fell short;
the low-lying fields did not flourish,
and the high-lying fields failed to ripen.
Grain prices will soar;
the people will die;
and the various kingdoms will raise armies.
They turned upon one another in mutual strife,
and their descendants were filled with fear.
King Mātaṅga replied to Pukkasāti:
These are the transformations resulting from the various constellations.
Now, I shall further explain that each of the twenty-eight lunar mansions has its own presiding influence.
As for the mansion named Ārdrā:
The Lord presides over neighboring kingdoms and the kingdom of Magadha;
as one who has been nurtured since his youth,
he shines universally upon the world.
The lunar mansion Mṛgaśiras presides over the country of Vidiśā;
the lunar mansion Ārdrā presides over the birth of portents.
He ruled over the kingdom of Pṛṣṭhāpura,
as well as the various brahmins and those whose wealth had increased.
Lord of the House of Gold and Jewels;
